sentences.text: ORDER With consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 16.05.2024, passed in M.A.C.C.
No.1703/2022 by the 26th Additional Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore, whereby a total sum of Rs.13,54,272/- has been awarded to them by way of compensation.

3. As per the appellants, on 04.03.2022 at about 7:40 p.m., respondent No.1 drove vehicle bearing registration No.TS-22-T-3622 which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against an auto rikshaw in which Lucky Panwar, daughter of appellant No.1 and sister of appellant No.2 was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6017 2 MA-6368-2024 travelling.
As a result of the accident, she suffered grievous injuries and was taken to the hospital for treatment, but eventually expired.
4. Thereafter, the appellants filed an application under Section 166 of the Act 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of compensation to them on account of death of Lucky Panwar.
The application was contested by respondent No.3/Insurance Company by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties, the Claims Tribunal has awarded Sangeeta vs Rakesh on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53918860/
1 compensation to the appellants as aforesaid.

5. This appeal for enhancement of the amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellants on the ground that the monthly income of the deceased which has been taken to be Rs.8,450/- per month is inordinately low.
She was in service and was also a State Level Wrestler.
Her income ought to have been assessed accordingly.
Since the appellants are two in number they ought to have been awarded amount for loss of consortium independently whereas the Claims Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.44,000/- only.
It is hence submitted that the amount of compensation awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.

6. Per Contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3, Insurance Company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellants in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.

8. From the evidence which has been brought on record by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:6017 3 MA-6368-2024 appellants, they have proved that the deceased was in service.
She was a State Level Wrestler.
At the time of her death, she was aged about 18 years hence had bright future prospects.
Since she was in service, her income ought to have been assessed atleast by considering her to be a semi-skilled worker.

Assessing the same accordingly, in view of the guidelines issued by the Labour Department of the State Government has income considering the fact that the accident took place in the year 2022 is assessed at Rs.9,500/- per month.
The appellants are two in number hence for loss of consortium, they ought to have been awarded amount separately whereas the Claims Tribunal has awarded the said amount to them joinly.
The same deserves to be assessed at Rs.88,000/-.
The amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal under the other heads is appropriate.

9. For loss of dependency the appellants would be entitled for an amount of Rs.9,500/- + Rs.3,800/-
(40% for future prospects of rise in income) which would be Rs.13,300/- per month i.e.
Rs.1,59,600/- annually.
The deduction of half made and multiplier of 18 applied by the Claims Tribunal is correct.
For loss of dependency, the appellants would be entitled for an amount of Rs.14,36,400/-.
For loss of consortium they would be entitled for a total sum of Rs.88,000/-.
10. The appellants are entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.15,57,400/- to them by way of compensation whereas the Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding them compensation of Rs.13,54,640/- only.

The appellants are hence held entitled for enhanced compensation amount of Rs.2,02,760/- which is rounded off to Rs.2,00,000/- as prayed by learned NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6017 4 MA-6368-2024 counsel for the appellants.
The said amount shall be paid to them alongwith the same rate of interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of payment.
11. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
